cards.power: Kd (Dissociation Constant) — Receptor Theory
cards.gradeReason: Affinity concept dressed as a wrestler; role clear but needs context to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Raccoon pharmacist holding receptor key. Mood: Cunning scientific.

cards.power: 34% of all approved targets — G-Protein Coupled Receptors
cards.gradeReason: Stat badge dominates; invites memorising a number, not embodying a character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Transformer serpent with seven transmembrane coils. Mood: All-powerful bureaucratic.

cards.power: 1 Transmembrane Domain — Transducer / Kinase
cards.gradeReason: Giraffe cascade image is fun; performer needs biochem frame to fully embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Giraffe handing signal down a chain. Mood: Relay-race urgent.

cards.power: Hours to Days (Onset) — Nuclear Receptor
cards.gradeReason: Onset stat as the main hook; genomic-slow is a concept, not a performance invitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Sloth drifting into cell nucleus. Mood: Inevitable glacial.

cards.power: Milliseconds (Speed) — Ligand-Gated Ion Channels
cards.gradeReason: Speed badge is vivid; the fast-gate role is graspable but needs the ion context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Electric eel bursting through gate. Mood: Lightning-fast reflex.

cards.power: pH 7.4 (150+ Local Anesthetics) — Active Potential Targets
cards.gradeReason: Use-dependent blockade concept is punchy; pH stat grounds the role well.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Electric eel wearing a pH meter crown. Mood: Controlled menacing.

cards.power: 100% Desensitization — Desensitization & Tolerance
cards.gradeReason: Phosphorylation mechanism — mechanistic description, no clear role to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Crab clamping shut a glowing receptor. Mood: Exhausted shutdown.

cards.power: cAMP, IP3/DAG, Ca2+ — PDE (The Degraders)
cards.gradeReason: Signal amplifier role is vivid; acronym list leans G3 but cascade energy saves it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Messenger rabbit amplifying tiny signal into explosion. Mood: Cascade frenzy.

cards.power: The Stop/Go Switch: Allosteric modulators bind to a different site than the agonist, changing the shape and effect of the receptor
cards.gradeReason: Padlock-and-key image is great; but modulator-not-agonist concept needs framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Chameleon twisting a lock sideways. Mood: Sneaky indirect control.

cards.power: EC50 (Potency) vs Emax (Efficacy) — Emax Preserved
cards.gradeReason: Curve-comparison card; explains a graph, does not invite anyone to BE anything.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Snake coiling into a sigmoid curve. Mood: Clinical inevitability.

cards.power: Bioavailability — F = [AUCoral / AUCiv]
cards.gradeReason: Formula-led card; bioavailability fraction is a number, not a character to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Salmon leaping through a flask waterfall. Mood: Determined uphill.

cards.power: The Gatekeeper: Drug absorbed from gut passes through portal vein to liver BEFORE reaching systemic circulation
cards.gradeReason: Gatekeeper role is immediately playable — bouncer at the liver door.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Bouncer bear blocking portal vein doorway. Mood: Impassive gatekeeping.

cards.power: Tissue Sink: High Vd means the drug hides in fat/muscle, making plasma levels a lie
cards.lore: Amiodarone is so famously tissue-bound that dialysis cannot remove it in an overdose
cards.gradeReason: Tissue-hider persona is clear; amiodarone lore is gold but needs the Vd frame.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Pufferfish stuffing drugs into fat tissue. Mood: Smugly hidden.

cards.power: The Reserve: Bound drug is inactive, cannot cross membranes, and cannot be excreted
cards.lore: In liver disease, the free fraction of highly bound drugs skyrockets, causing toxicity at normal levels
cards.gradeReason: Reserve keeper role is solid; liver disease lore adds real clinical bite.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Kangaroo hoarding pills in her pouch. Mood: Protectively inactive.

cards.power: The Decay: Time to eliminate half the drug. Depends on both Clearance and Volume of Distribution
cards.lore: It takes 5 half-lives to reach steady state, regardless of dosing frequency
cards.gradeReason: Decay persona works; 5x t½ rule is beautifully quotable, saves this from G3.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Axolotl melting in half under a countdown clock. Mood: Elegiac steady.

cards.power: Enzyme Saturation: Eliminates fixed AMOUNT per unit time, regardless of concentration
cards.lore: Phenytoin and alcohol follow zero-order kinetics. A small dose increase can cause a catastrophic spike
cards.gradeReason: HUMBUG! chaos king — non-linear menace is immediately playable at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Sloth on treadmill while bottles pile up behind. Mood: Catastrophically calm.

cards.power: The Washout: The volume of blood cleared of drug per unit time
cards.lore: Drugs with high renal clearance require strict dose reduction in renal failure to prevent toxic accumulation
cards.gradeReason: Beaver-dam clearance metaphor lands; eGFR <30 Metformin stat is clinically sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Beaver flushing drug molecules through kidney dam. Mood: Vigilant purging.

cards.power: The Microenzyme: The superfamily of enzymes that decides the fate of your drugs
cards.lore: CYP2C9 metabolises warfarin; CYP2D6 metabolises codeine; CYP3A4 metabolises half of everything
cards.gradeReason: Chief of the liver underworld — fateful, immediate, fully embodiable persona.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Cockroach crime boss in liver factory. Mood: Omnipotent casually powerful.

cards.power: Gene Upregulation: Forces the liver to build more enzymes, destroying substrate drugs faster
cards.lore: Rifampicin + OCP = unintended pregnancy. Takes days to weeks to start and stop
cards.gradeReason: The saboteur who burns drugs before they work — vivid, immediate, table-ready energy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Squirrel setting drug conveyor belt on fire. Mood: Enthusiastic destruction.

cards.power: The Blockade: Competes for the CYP active site, causing substrate drug levels to spike dangerously
cards.lore: Statin + CYP3A4 inhibitors = massive rhabdomyolysis risk. Effect is immediate upon dosing
cards.gradeReason: Immediate-effect blocker with lethal consequences — rhabdo lore makes this unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Badger jamming its body into enzyme doorway. Mood: Ruthlessly blocking.

cards.power: Pharmacogenomics — ~7% Poor Metabolizers
cards.gradeReason: 263 variants stat-dump; interesting concept but no clear role to perform at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Chameleon DNA helix in different colors. Mood: Unpredictably genetic.

cards.power: Timing Is Everything: Only used for drugs where the gap between toxic and therapeutic is dangerously small
cards.lore: Trough timing is most accurate. Vancomycin, lithium and digoxin — without monitoring, you are guessing
cards.gradeReason: Owl-with-magnifying-glass persona is sharp; Narrow TI Only is a clear role signal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Owl nurse watching drug level graph on tightrope. Mood: Hyper-vigilant.

cards.power: The Adrenaline Surge: High heart rate, constricts smooth muscle and dilates bronchioles. The fist pump of the autonomic system
cards.lore: a1 constricts vessels, b1 fires the heart, b2 opens the lungs
cards.gradeReason: Fight! Fight! Fight! — you know exactly what energy to bring the moment you read it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Flaming cheetah throwing punches with adrenaline fists. Mood: Pure adrenalized fury.

cards.power: The Sloth: Slows heart rate, contracts smooth muscle, stimulates glandular secretion
cards.lore: M1 is CNS/cognitive, M2 slows the heart, M3 opens the glands and gut
cards.gradeReason: Rest & Digest sloth persona — instantly, bodily playable. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Sloth digesting in a hammock with slow heartbeat monitor. Mood: Profoundly calm.

cards.power: The Muscle Deity: ACh releases from motor nerve, binds NM nicotinic receptors. Without NMJ, you cannot breathe
cards.lore: Botulinum blocks SNARE. Levetiracetam binds SV2A. Disrupting the NMJ has catastrophic effects
cards.gradeReason: Cannot-breathe consequence is visceral; SV2A/SNARE targets are compelling but obscure.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Frog conductor sparking neuromuscular junction. Mood: Electrically urgent.

cards.power: Alpha-Adrenoceptor Drugs — First-Dose Hypotension
cards.gradeReason: First-dose hypotension warning is clinically vivid; a1/a2 split gives clear performer options.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Dog fainting dramatically on first pill. Mood: Sudden floor-bound surprise.

cards.power: The Cardiotamer: Blocks b1 in the heart. Reduces HR, contractility, conduction. Anti-hypertensive, anti-arrhythmic, anti-anginal
cards.lore: Non-selective b-blockers mask hypoglycaemia. Metoprolol and bisoprolol are b1-selective and safer in asthma
cards.gradeReason: Stop-sign bear with clear role — cardiotamer is immediately performable, hypoglycaemia lore is sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Bear holding a stop sign in front of a racing heart. Mood: Firm steady control.

cards.power: Antimuscarinic — Tertiary vs Quaternary
cards.lore: Tertiary crosses BBB — cognitive effects. Quaternary (ipratropium) stays in the periphery
cards.gradeReason: Two-tier character concept is memorable; BBB-crossing distinction is clinically useful.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Camel split as two halves — one in brain, one in lung. Mood: Divided purposeful.

cards.power: The Emergency Switch: b-agonist receptor position for cardiac resuscitation, septic shock. Adrenaline, noradrenaline, dopamine
cards.lore: At low dose, dopamine dilates renal arteries. At high dose, it is pure a1 vasoconstriction. Dose is everything
cards.gradeReason: Emergency Switch is immediately embodiable — dose-determines-character drama is table gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Octopus ECG paddles in ICU chaos. Mood: Code-blue urgency.

cards.power: The Multiplier: Blocks ACh breakdown, amplifying cholinergic signal. Used in myasthenia gravis, Alzheimers, reversal of NMJ blockade
cards.lore: Organophosphates do this irreversibly. SLUDGE: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI distress, Emesis
cards.gradeReason: SLUDGE acronym is quotable and performative; amplifier role is clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Trash bin overflowing with ACh molecules. Mood: Uncontrolled excess.

cards.power: Too Much Drug — Miosis (Key Sign)
cards.gradeReason: Crisis mode is immediately embodiable — SLUDGE chaos performance starts on reading.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Ram with pinpoint pupils drowning in secretions. Mood: Overwhelming flood.

cards.power: The Signal Failure: Inadequate NMJ activation. Clinical emergency requiring ICU admission and ventilatory support
cards.gradeReason: Worsening Weakness is immediately playable — sagging, failing, opposite energy to Cholinergic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Ram collapsing under its own weight. Mood: Worsening silent emergency.

cards.power: The Countermeasure: The body adapts via enzyme induction, receptor downregulation, altered transporter expression
cards.gradeReason: Chameleon adapting — immediately embodiable character who neutralises every move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Chameleon turning the same colour as a pill bottle. Mood: Adaptive indifferent.

cards.power: Competitive antagonists can be overcome by adding more agonist. Non-competitive antagonists cannot — they drop the Emax
cards.gradeReason: Shift Right vs Drop Down metaphor is excellent; competitive/non split is a clear wrestling move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Donkey pushing a dose-response curve sideways. Mood: Implacably resistant.

cards.power: Drug Combinations — 1 + 1 = 3
cards.gradeReason: Synergy formula is catchy; drug-combination partner role works at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Beaver and squirrel fusing into supersized creature. Mood: Multiplicative joy.

cards.power: The Safety Margin: TI = TD50 / ED50. Narrow TI = warfarin, digoxin, lithium, aminoglycosides
cards.lore: Lithium has a TI barely above 1. Toxic above 1.5mmol/L. The safety margin is tissue-thin
cards.gradeReason: Tissue-thin safety margin is visceral; lithium lore is a great clinical hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Mouse balancing between two cliffs labelled toxic and therapeutic. Mood: Precarious.

cards.power: The Consciousness Threshold: Lower MAC = more potent inhalational agent. Requires synergists like N2O and opioids to reduce MAC
cards.gradeReason: MAC as wrestling stat is clever; inhalational agents persona works but needs context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Owl anaesthetist with gas mask above unconscious patient. Mood: Precise controlled sleep.

cards.power: Sleeper Agent: Codeine needs CYP2D6 to become morphine. Clopidogrel needs CYP2C19 to become its active thiol
cards.lore: CYP2D6 poor metabolizers get no analgesia from codeine. Ultra-rapid metabolizers risk respiratory arrest. BOTH are dangerous
cards.gradeReason: Sleeper Agent persona is evocative; poor metabolizer/ultra-rapid split is genuinely alarming lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Butterfly emerging from grey pill cocoon into active drug. Mood: Latent dangerous.

cards.power: The Infinite Loop: Drug excreted in bile, reaches the intestine, gets reactivated by gut bacteria, reabsorbed. Extends drug half-life
cards.lore: Ethinylestradiol cycles through enterohepatic circulation. Gut flora disruption (antibiotics) can reduce OCP levels
cards.gradeReason: Infinite loop is a concept diagram, not a performable invitation — G3 despite vivid OCP lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Drug molecule on infinite loop waterslide through gut and liver. Mood: Endlessly cycling.

cards.power: The Dual Patient: Drug crosses placenta via simple diffusion. Small, lipophilic, non-ionised drugs cross best. Risk depends on timing
cards.lore: Valproate causes neural tube defects. ACE inhibitors in trimester 2/3 cause renal dysgenesis. Warfarin causes fetal warfarin syndrome
cards.gradeReason: Dual-patient frame is compelling; teratogen lore is sobering and memorable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Kangaroo joey inside pouch with tiny danger sign. Mood: Protective yet alarmed.

cards.power: COX Inhibition — 7-10 Days (Aspirin)
cards.gradeReason: Irreversible COX-blocker persona is clear; GI-bleed risk makes Neil a double-edged character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Beaver blocking COX enzyme with wrench, stomach smouldering. Mood: Reliably risky.

cards.power: PPI — ~18 Hours (Pump Regen)
cards.lore: Once inactivated, the pump cannot regenerate for ~18 hours. Take before first meal
cards.gradeReason: 18-hour pump regen is a vivid stat; pre-meal timing instruction is immediately useful.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Snake coiled around a proton pump valve, sealing it shut. Mood: Irreversibly sealed.

cards.power: Anticoagulation — INR 2.0-3.0 (Goal)
cards.lore: Warfarin is metabolised by CYP2C9. S-warfarin is 3-4x more potent than R-warfarin. INR 2-3 for AF, DVT
cards.gradeReason: INR tightrope is a vivid performance frame; S/R warfarin potency split is genuinely surprising lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Hedgehog walking vitamin K tightrope with INR meter. Mood: Nervously calibrated.

cards.power: Renal Clearance — 25% Filtered Na+ (Loop)
cards.gradeReason: Elephant flushing sodium is a clear image; loop/thiazide split gives performer options.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Elephant spraying sodium out of nephron tube. Mood: Forceful liquid clearance.

cards.power: HMG-CoA Reductase — >50% LDL Reduction
cards.lore: Rosuvastatin is generally CYP3A4-spared (reducing interactions). Rhabdomyolysis risk increases with CYP inhibitors
cards.gradeReason: Hepatic saboteur persona is fun; rhabdo lore gives teeth to a boring lipid card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Beaver sabotaging cholesterol factory assembly line. Mood: Methodical destruction.

cards.power: Analgesic — 10mg IV = 30mg Oral
cards.lore: Buprenorphine is a partial agonist — if you give to a heroin addict, it triggers withdrawal. 10mg IV morphine = 30mg oral
cards.gradeReason: Equianalgesic ratio is table-useful; buprenorphine withdrawal-trigger lore is genuinely dramatic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Sloth on drip with floating mu-receptor crown. Mood: Blissfully dangerous.

cards.power: Selective Toxicity — 8 Distinct Mechanisms / PK/PD Targets
cards.gradeReason: Selective toxicity concept is vivid; 8-mechanism badge skews descriptive but character is clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Octopus attacking bacterial cell with eight different weapons. Mood: Precisely targeted chaos.

cards.power: Static vs Cidal — 2 MIC vs MBC
cards.gradeReason: Static-vs-cidal split is a clear binary persona; turtle vs bactericidal rabbit is memorable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Tortoise holding a static flag vs rabbit with kill sign. Mood: Decisive clinical choice.

cards.power: ESbL Hydrolysate Gate — Bacterial Evasion
cards.gradeReason: Bacterial escape artist persona is clear; ESBL/efflux/target-modification triad is solid.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Bacteria soldier in armour deflecting antibiotic arrows. Mood: Entrenched defiant.

cards.power: Viral Targets — Selective Activation (TK)
cards.gradeReason: Viral-TK-activation concept is elegant; chameleon artwork signals selectivity well.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Chameleon activating only inside infected cell. Mood: Precisely selective.

cards.power: AntiFungals — CYP51 (Demethylase)
cards.lore: Azoles are potent CYP3A4 inhibitors in humans. Fluconazole + warfarin = massive INR spike. Use with caution
cards.gradeReason: Fluconazole-warfarin INR spike lore is a table-stopping moment; CYP51 hook is specific.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Mole digging into fungal cell wall with CYP51 pickaxe. Mood: Targeted demolition.

cards.power: Cytotoxics — S-Phase Specificity
cards.gradeReason: S-phase replication killer is a clear role; bone marrow toxicity shadow gives clinical gravitas.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Rhinoceros charging into cancer cell DNA replication fork. Mood: Collateral necessary.

cards.power: Cascade Prescribing: Drug causes side effect, treated by drug...
cards.lore: 5+ drugs in the elderly causes cognitive decline, and GI bleeds. Depression...
cards.gradeReason: Accumulation concept is important but the card describes a problem rather than inviting a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Raccoon buried under avalanche of pill bottles. Mood: Overwhelmed helpless.

cards.power: The Underfoot Guest: St John's Wort and herb-drug interactions
cards.lore: St John's Wort induces CYP3A4. Grapefruit irreversibly inhibits it
cards.gradeReason: Grapefruit-inhibits lore is famous and great; but the card is a warning notice, not a persona.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: Hedgehog with grapefruit and herb bundle blocking CYP. Mood: Innocently destructive.

verdict: Uncle FrizzleBob delivers Pharmacology Vol 02 with the same loveable cast of mnemonic animals, enzymes, and lab-coat chaos-merchants that made MedKayfab famous. Stars of the show: Cyp the CYP450 Chief, Indie the Inducer, and Inhi the Inhibitor — a criminal trio that owns every pharmacology exam. Weak spots are the curve-and-formula cards (Dose the Dose-Response, Abby Absorption, Poly the Polymorphism) that explain rather than invite, dragging G1 below the 35% target. The END OF THE LINE finale page with its Clinical Toxidrome Final Quest is a genuine table moment and a beautiful payoff. Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: For medical students who want pharmacology to stop reading like a textbook and start feeling like a wrestling card game. 54 mnemonic characters land the mechanism and the memory cue in one punch.

marketingText:
MedKayfab: PHARMACOKINETICS – What the Body Does to the Drug (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

54 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master first-pass metabolism and the CYP450 enzymes, the inducers and inhibitors that quietly rewrite a dose, and the zero-order kinetics that turn a steady habit into a slow overdose.

You learned the drug. Did anyone teach you what the body does to it after a patient swallows it?

Here is the gap that ends up on an incident report. You can know every agent on the formulary cold and still poison a patient, because the dose that was safe on Monday becomes a toxic level on Thursday the moment a colleague adds an antibiotic that jams the enzyme clearing it. Pharmacokinetics is the half of pharmacology nobody can see on the prescription: how fast the liver chews a drug up, how the kidney lets it go, and why the same milligram that helps one patient stacks up in the next until it stops their heart. It stays invisible right up to the point it is the only thing that matters.

MedKayfab Pharmacokinetics puts the body's drug-handling machinery in the ring, where the enzymes, the kinetics, and the interactions decide who walks out. You learn metabolism by watching it turn on a patient, not by reciting a clearance table you will have forgotten by the ward round.

YOU'LL GET
- 54 illustrated MedKayfab cards (15pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (including the Quest Die and the Clinical Toxidrome final scenario)
- S-Tier characters like Cyp the CYP450 Chief, Indie the Inducer, and Zero the Zero-Order
- Free lifetime updates as the interaction tables and guidelines shift
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence, print, share, and adapt freely
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
This is the metabolism-and-kinetics half of the MedKayfab Pharmacology series, the companion to the named-drug roster in The Synaptic Arsenal. You will meet Cyp the CYP450 Chief, the liver enzyme boss who sets the speed limit on how fast a drug leaves the body and whose mood decides whether a standard dose is therapy or overdose. Indie the Inducer spends days quietly building more of those enzymes, so a dose that worked last week barely registers this week, and a transplant drug or a contraceptive fails without a single new symptom to warn you. Zero the Zero-Order runs at a fixed ceiling: past it, every extra milligram piles up instead of clearing, the kinetics hiding behind ethanol, phenytoin, and the overdose that arrives in slow motion. The deck closes on Polypharmacy and Herb the Herbal in a Clinical Toxidrome finale, where every interaction you skipped comes back to collect.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor built for the moment you need it under pressure. You get the Character (the mnemonic), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (the half-life, the route, the interaction risk), the Lore (the clinical story), and the Quest (the prescribing challenge). The Mechanism Flash mode is unforgiving with kinetics: if you cannot say in one sentence why this drug and that drug should never share a chart, the patient on the Stage finds out for you.

Honest cognitive load
This is a mid-to-high intensity deck for medical and pharmacy students learning ADME and drug interactions, and for anyone re-sitting pharmacology for the boards. It assumes you already know a few drugs by name, which is exactly why it pairs best with Essential Pharmacology: The Synaptic Arsenal for the roster, with Internal Medicine for the polypharmacy patient who is on nine of them at once, and with Laboratory Medicine for the levels you will be chasing.

ABOUT MEDKAYFAB
MedKayfab is a narrative medical learning card game, 50 decks covering the full medical curriculum. Every card encodes a clinical mechanism as a character with a personality, a story, and a reasoning challenge. Built by a physician. Assembled with AI tools. Manually revised. Honest about its limitations. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

PAY WHAT YOU WANT
This deck is Pay What You Want, including free.
If you find it useful: a fair price is €5. If you're a student on a budget: enter €0. No questions asked. If you want to support more decks: anything above fair price is appreciated.
CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

DISCLAIMER
MedKayfab is a learning companion, not a clinical reference. Content was created by a physician and reviewed to the best of our knowledge, but medicine evolves, guidelines change, and some mechanisms in here will be simplified or wrong. Always verify against current primary sources and clinical guidelines before applying anything to patient care, and never make a dosing or interaction decision from a card. The Blödsinn! is the vehicle. The science is serious.

Stay fluffy. — Doc FrizzleBob
